replies.author: @VagariousTravel-868
replies.text: I understand your frustration. You're raising a real point about the mismatch between what we see happening on coastlines and the timelines we hear about in geology. But the evidence for deep time comes from many independent sources, radiometric dating, plate tectonics, the fossil record, and measured erosion rates that are consistent across different fields. The problem with the coastal homes isn't that erosion rates are wrong. It's that homes were built on land that was already eroding. In California, the Coastal Commission denied permits on some of those lots decades ago, citing wave hazards. The warnings were there. The issue isn't the science. It's that people built anyway.
